name: AI6YM PicoFox (RP2040 + SI5351, 2 m FM)
radio: SI5351 clock generator (TCXO) + amplifier; FM by retuning the PLL per audio sample

design.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (hardware and vendor firmware; not included here)

flash.bootloader_instructions: The PicoFox's BOOTSEL button (SW2) is inside the enclosure; the switch on the side is power. With the fox on and plugged in, use "Reboot into bootloader" here (the Arduino 1200-baud touch on its serial port, which both the vendor firmware and fox-bench's answer): a drive called RPI-RP2 appears.

usb.label: vendor firmware
usb.when: vendor firmware (Arduino RP2040 core: Adafruit's generic TinyUSB ids), drive 'PicoFox' + serial — seen on a rev 3 board

usb.label: fox-bench firmware
usb.when: fox-bench firmware (foxlib-c): drive FOXBENCH + serial console

pins.name: GP0
pins.note: I2C SDA to SI5351 (shared with the attenuator data line)

revisions.r3: BVA1761 attenuator, 0–127 steps of about 0.25 dB

battery.divider_note: Internal LiPo; about five hours at 100 % duty. Charges over USB only with the power switch ON. No battery telemetry is available to the page.

notes: The firmware's Morse table is A–Z and 0–9 only: anything else in the callsign (/, -, space) is silently dropped from the ID it generates. fox-bench writes its own ID audio instead, so the full message is sent, but the CALLSIGN setting is still reduced to those characters.
A DUTY_CYCLE of 0, an empty callsign, or a frequency within 20 kHz of a band edge does not produce an error on the board — the fox just stays silent.

Each segment (audio, then ID) goes out on a different carrier offset: 0, +1, +3, +5, +3, +1, 0, −1, −3, −5, −3, −1 kHz in turn. With a duty cycle under 100 %, rev 3 boards also step the attenuation base / +10 dB / +5 dB each cycle. Both are firmware behaviour, not settings.
Silence inside audio.wav is an unmodulated carrier, still on the air. Only the duty-cycle gap is actually off.
Firmware updates and the stock-firmware restore are UF2 files copied to the RPI-RP2 drive. The PicoFox does not run CircuitPython.

serial.notes: USB serial prints boot messages only: 'Revision: N', 'Detected settings change, generating new callsign audio', 'si5351 setup complete.' There is no command interface.
